register_row: ADM-02 (unchanged; this applies rulings recorded under it, it does not re-flip it)

rulings_applied.1_channel_page: Hide a muted or blocked account's videos on the account's OWN channel page too. Applied server-side, so it survives a hard reload.
rulings_applied.2_autosuggest: Autosuggest stays viewer-agnostic server-side (vidra-search's index stores static eligibility and never per-viewer state, which is what makes the ranked-ids contract visibility-safe); the FRONTEND drops the channel suggestions naming a muted or blocked account.
rulings_applied.3_controls: A shared mute/block control on the channel and profile pages, reusing the existing API and the comment menu's idiom.
rulings_applied.4_copy: The settings copy stays as ruled; only the two empty states that said LESS than their own page headers were corrected.

lab.topology: one origin — a pipe-only node proxy on 127.0.0.1:3200 in front of `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3100 and vidra-core on :8088 — because vidra_refresh is SameSite=Lax with Path=/api/v1/auth
lab.postgres: native PostgreSQL 16 on a private port (55432, -k /tmp), fresh cluster, core migrated to schema 131
lab.redis: native redis on a private port (56379)
lab.vidra_search: native on :8089 at search schema 18 with its own database; core wired to it (instance reports service_enabled=true, suggestions_enabled=true), so every suggestion payload below came from the real service
lab.frontend: production `next build` served from .next/standalone with .next/static and public copied in; Node 24.4.1 (vitest is broken on Node 25 in this repo)
lab.browser: real Chromium against that origin, hard reloads between states
lab.binaries: TWO — origin/main (8372a57) for the paired baseline, and the patched branch, swapped over the SAME database and fixtures
lab.fixture_honesty: the four videos are DB-published rows with no media bytes: created through POST /channels/{handle}/videos (state=draft) and flipped to state='published' with SQL. Every surface under test is a LIST PREDICATE that reads privacy/state and the mute tables and never the bytes, so the missing media cannot flatter the result — the 'No preview' placeholders in the screenshots are that, and nothing else. Leftover rows from the tagged integration lane were purged before the measurements (4 users, 4 videos remained).

SC1_channel_page.list_and_count_agree: asserted on every read: a page returning no rows while the total still promised 1 would promise a page the list cannot serve
SC1_channel_page.probe_guard: every viewer-scoped probe asserts GET /auth/me = 200 first — every discovery route is optionalAuth, so an expired bearer is silently anonymous

SC1_sibling_channel_reads.GET /channels/{handle}: 200 unchanged for the muter — the header, the handle, the follower count and the display name all still render. DELIBERATE: a mute is not a disappearance, and the header is the only route to the control that lifts it.
SC1_sibling_channel_reads.GET /channels/{handle}/stats: 404 for the muter — requireAuth + owner/editor only, reported as 404 so existence is not leaked. No gap; unreachable for a non-owner.
SC1_sibling_channel_reads.GET /channels/{handle}/live: 403 for the muter — requireAuth + canManageChannelContent. No gap; unreachable for a non-owner.
SC1_sibling_channel_reads.GET /channels/{handle}/donation-addresse: 200, NO auth middleware at all and no viewer. The Support button therefore stays on a muted account's channel header. Coherent with the header staying, and out of this slice's scope — recorded, not widened.
SC1_sibling_channel_reads.channel playlists: NO SUCH ROUTE. `git grep` over internal/httpapi/server.go finds only POST /playlists, GET /me/playlists and GET /playlists/{id}; nothing lists a channel's playlists, and ChannelView's own comment says so. Nothing to fix.
SC1_sibling_channel_reads.GET /live (the public 'Live now' rail): optionalAuth but takes NO VIEWER: handleListLivePublicStreams calls livesvc.ListLivePublic(ctx, limit, offset). A muted account's live stream would still be listed to the muter. Read from the code, not measured (the lab has no live stream). Recorded, not widened.

server_side_unchanged.measured: with uma's mute in place, the payload for uma, for cleo and for an anonymous caller is BYTE-IDENTICAL

SC2_suggestions.mechanism: the client cannot map a suggestion to an account without help — a suggestion carries channel_handle for a channel and video_id for a video, and the mute/block lists carried only user_id/username. Both lists now carry the account's channel_handles (one ARRAY() subquery; no new route, no new query), so the frontend builds the hidden-handle set ONCE per settled session and every keystroke is free.

findings_recorded_not_fixed: GET /live (the public 'Live now' rail) takes no viewer at all, so a muted account's live stream is still listed to the muter. Read from the code; the lab had no live stream.
GET /channels/{handle}/donation-addresses is unauthenticated and unfiltered, so the Support button stays on a muted account's channel header.

A muted account's VIDEO-title suggestions still appear. Not a decision: a video suggestion carries only video_id, so no client-side filter can reach it — and a mute never hid a direct watch URL either (A16 slice 3's table: watch detail 200 for every actor).
Neither the new menu nor the comment menu reports a FAILED mute or block; the label simply does not flip. A gap they share.

A muted account's profile page still lists its CHANNELS. The channel cards link to pages that are now empty for the muter, so nothing the mute hides is reachable through them, but the names are still on screen — the same shape as the FOLLOWING sidebar rail A16 slice 3 recorded.

The suggestion filter's optimistic handle update is additive: unmuting drops only the handles the calling page names, so a channel this session never saw can stay in the hidden set until the next session's read. The safe direction — one suggestion missing, never one appearing that should not.
